haiku-low.q1: Keys load at startup, before /healthz can return 200. The pod becomes ready only after all three keys are in memory.
haiku-low.q2: It retries 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then exits non-zero. The pod never becomes ready, the rollout halts, and old pods keep serving traffic.
haiku-low.q3: Every 5 minutes it re-reads all three secrets. A successful read replaces the value. A failed read keeps the last good value, logs a warning with name and version id, and retries next refresh.
haiku-low.q4: Key values are held in process memory only. They must never go on disk, into environment variables, or into logs.
haiku-low.q5: Only the orders-api-prod identity can read prod values, read-only. Only the security on-call can write them. Engineers cannot read prod values.
haiku-low.q6: Git history keeps the old values and images still contain them, so they count as leaked. They become harmless only when revoked at the provider in step 7.
haiku-low.q7: Clients call secrets.get(name) on every request. It reads memory only, so the refreshed value is used on the next request without a restart.
haiku-low.q8: The operator checks each pod's /healthz at its own address. Every pod must show the new version id for that key before revoking the old key.
haiku-low.q9: Set store access, copy keys into the store, change code and config (switch clients, remove keys from config), deploy and verify, then rotate keys at providers.
haiku-low.q10: make run sets APP_ENV=dev and loads orders-api/dev/* using the developer's own dev access. Developers never need prod access, and prod keys are never used.
haiku-low.q11: The process exits with a non-zero code. It never runs with partial keys, so the pod never becomes ready.

sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded into memory first; /healthz returns 200 (ready) only after all three keys are loaded.
sonnet.q2: It retries 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then exits with a non-zero code and never becomes ready. The rollout halts and old pods keep serving, so live traffic is unaffected.
sonnet.q3: A refresh every 5 minutes re-reads all three secrets; each successful read replaces the in-memory value in one step. If a read fails, that secret keeps its last good value, a warning (secret name and version id, no value) is logged, it retries at the next refresh, and /healthz is unchanged.
sonnet.q4: Held in process memory only. They must never go on disk, into environment variables, or into logs (version ids may be logged).
sonnet.q5: Read: the orders-api-prod service identity (read-only on orders-api/prod/*). Write: only the security on-call. Engineers cannot read prod values.
sonnet.q6: Git history is not rewritten, so the old keys remain in history and are treated as leaked. Each key is replaced (rotated) at its provider and the old key is revoked once every running pod uses the new one, making the old values harmless.
sonnet.q7: Clients (PaymentsClient, EmailClient, GeocodingClient) call secrets.get(name) on every request, which reads from memory, so the refreshed value is used on the next request with no restart.
sonnet.q8: The person running the rotation checks each pod directly at its own address (not via the service); each pod's /healthz secret_versions must show the new version id (from the store write) for that key. If any pod shows the old version, check again later and do not revoke.
sonnet.q9: 1) Set store access; 2) copy keys into the store; 3) change code/config (switch app to read from store and remove api_key lines from config/app.yaml), then deploy and verify; 6) rotate keys at providers; 7) revoke old keys.
sonnet.q10: From the secret store at orders-api/dev/* (APP_ENV=dev set by make run), using sandbox keys and the developer's own dev access; no prod access or fallback to prod keys.
sonnet.q11: The load fails because a key is missing, so the process exits with a non-zero code. It never runs with partial keys and never becomes ready.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. Security has not decided on a rotation schedule; no cadence is set in the plan.
